mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last three weeks (-4.3, -9.6, -17.3, -14.4), reflecting an entrenched substitution away from discretionary outings. This momentum persists mechanically because households that have adopted reduced-shopping routines do not revert without an external trigger, so the four-week forward mean continues below the trailing four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined week-over-week for 3 of the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the trailing 28-day mean, i.e., the decline trend reverses despite no change in other series.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has fallen sharply to -20.7 at t-0w after crossing the -20 threshold at t-1w, indicating commuters and shoppers are avoiding public transit hubs that feed retail precincts. Once TRANSIT breaches -20, retail footfall near transit nodes drops further over the following two weeks as transit-dependent shopping trips are suppressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -21.3 at t-1w and -20.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -20, indicating the transit-retail linkage has decoupled.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compound each other: fewer people commuting (WORKPLACES down to -7.7) combined with reduced transit usage (-20.7) eliminates both the work-adjacent and transit-adjacent retail trips that together drive a large share of retail footfall, producing a sharper joint decline in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fell every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no larger than what WORKPLACES alone or TRANSIT alone would predict in isolation, i.e., no super-additive effect observed.

mechanism_narrative: The steady rise in RESIDENTIAL (1.0 to 6.3 over four weeks) signals accelerating stay-at-home behavior consistent with anticipated government restriction announcements. In a tightening-restrictions regime, this residential rise precedes further formal closures of retail and recreation venues, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the subsequent four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 1.0 to 6.3 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or flattens over the next 4 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to climb, indicating the anticipated policy linkage did not materialize.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility partially rebounded from -18.9 at t-1w to -5.3 at t-0w, suggesting households are substituting outdoor recreation for indoor retail visits as a lower-risk activity. This substitution effect should produce a short-term further dip in RETAIL_REC over the next week as outdoor options continue to absorb recreational demand.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved by 13.6 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with PARKS over the next week rather than falling, indicating no substitution effect between the two categories.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained near flat (0.0 to 0.3) over the last two weeks after an earlier spike, indicating stockpiling behavior has stabilized. Stabilized essential-goods demand frees no additional discretionary spending capacity, so RETAIL_REC continues its downward trajectory rather than recovering over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM flattened to 0.0 and 0.3 in the last two weeks after a 6.6 spike
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, showing the stockpiling-stabilization link does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility crosses above 6 percent while WORKPLACES simultaneously stays below -7, this combination signals an imminent formal lockdown order is already being behaviorally anticipated by the population; once this joint threshold is crossed, government-mandated retail closures follow within weeks, driving RETAIL_REC sharply lower.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 6 and WORKPLACES < -7 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 6.3 and WORKPLACES reached -7.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further over the next 4 weeks even though both thresholds are crossed, indicating the anticipated policy-driven closure effect is absent.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-March marks the transition into Sydney's autumn, when cooler, wetter weather typically reduces outdoor park usage and shifts recreational activity indoors toward retail and entertainment venues under normal seasonal patterns. However, with PARKS already suppressed by behavioral avoidance, any seasonal uplift that would normally redirect activity to RETAIL_REC is overridden, so the autumn seasonal effect fails to produce a rise in RETAIL_REC this year.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains deeply negative at -5.3 despite partial rebound, inconsistent with normal autumn indoor-shift seasonality
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks in line with typical autumn seasonal indoor-shift patterns, showing the pandemic override did not suppress the seasonal effect.
